company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps came in at +1.6%, well below the consensus of +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll delivered solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — clean EPS was approximately 42 cents. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the consensus of $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS band of $1.85–2.15 was left unchanged and FQ2 EPS guidance is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings extensive CFO experience, having previously held that role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership change rather than an operational or financial catalyst.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the consensus of 13.85%, despite revenue of $2.311 billion coming in slightly above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets, and expects a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal 2027 without providing formal guidance yet. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost-reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a significant data readout that reinforces VK2735's competitive positioning in the increasingly crowded but high-growth obesity drug market. This is a major near-term catalyst for the stock.

sectors: The RV sector faces ongoing headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and persistent inflation are keeping retail soft. The GLP-1/obesity drug space gets a fresh positive data point from Viking Therapeutics. Cognex's RealSense acquisition signals continued investment in physical AI and robotics perception.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, with several before-the-open reports worth walking through.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street at fifty-four dollars and three cents — but the quality of that beat is questionable. The outperformance was driven by tariff refunds providing a 145 basis point tailwind to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding another 105 basis points. Underneath that, domestic comps came in at plus 1.6 percent, well short of the consensus of plus 3.1 percent, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management struck a modestly constructive tone, noting sales improved in the final eight weeks of the quarter versus the first eight. This is a mixed print — headline beat, weak internals.

Cognex is making a significant move into physical AI, announcing the acquisition of RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus an additional 106 and a half million. RealSense is projected to generate 80 to 90 million dollars in revenue with more than 50 percent year-over-year growth. This is a strategically bullish step for Cognex into the robotics and physical AI buildout theme.

MillerKnoll posted a solid fiscal first quarter — 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents — and importantly, even stripping out the 11-cent tariff refund benefit, the company still beat at roughly 42 cents clean. Sales missed at 923 million versus 943 million expected, but orders were up 3.5 percent year-over-year. Full-year revenue guidance was trimmed slightly while the earnings per share band was held unchanged. This is a generally positive print with a minor revenue caveat.

THOR Industries disappointed. Fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share came in at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4 percent. Management's tone was cautious — calling out stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation squeezing consumer budgets throughout the key selling season. They expect a roughly flat retail environment in fiscal 2027 and won't give formal guidance until later in the fall. There were some silver linings — dealer inventory is healthy and North American towable RV order backlog surged about 75 percent year-over-year — but the overall print and commentary skew bearish.

Finally, the standout mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking in pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 obesity drug VK2735, showing 22 percent weight loss. This is a meaningful data readout that strengthens Viking's competitive position in the obesity drug space and is a clear bullish catalyst for the stock.

Pentair separately announced a CFO transition, naming Bob Hau — previously CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox — effective November 1st. More of a housekeeping item than a market mover.

Bottom line for today: the tape is being driven by individual earnings stories. Viking is the high-beta momentum name to watch on the GLP-1 theme. AutoZone's beat needs to be contextualized against weak comps. And THOR's cautious macro commentary on the consumer is worth flagging as a broader read-through on rate-sensitive discretionary spending.
